display_name: List every live peer on this solet
description: No-MCP peer enumeration: a global, unfiltered snapshot of every peer currently registered on this solet, callable without a registered bridge. Takes no arguments — this is a global snapshot, identical for every caller, so there is nothing to scope by. Returns 'agent_ids', the sorted list of distinct agent_id kinds present (e.g. 'claude_code', 'codex'), and 'instances', a map from each agent_id to the list of its live instances. Each instance carries six fields: agent_instance_id (the durable per-bridge routing key), session_label (human-facing display name), parent_pid, registered_at (a deprecated alias for created_at, kept one release), created_at, and updated_at (bumped by dispatch activity — the closest thing to a last-active timestamp). Two fields present on the underlying registry row are deliberately NOT exposed here: bridge_id and agent_session_id. Both are routing/identity fields one peer could use to address or impersonate another's transport, and this verb preserves the exact field-set precedent of the two pre-existing MCP surfaces (the localhost /peer/list HTTP route and the Streamable-HTTP MCP tool) rather than widening it for the no-MCP path. This closes the companion gap peer_inbox left open: peer_inbox let a no-MCP session read its OWN mail, but that same session had no way to see who else was live to send mail TO.
embedding_description: See which other agents are currently registered and live on this solet right now — their agent kind, instance id, session label, and process id — grouped by agent kind, without needing an MCP session, a registered bridge, or a peer_list HTTP call.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: agent_ids: the sorted list of distinct agent_id kinds with at least one live instance. instances: a map from each agent_id to its list of live instances, each carrying agent_instance_id, session_label, parent_pid, registered_at (deprecated alias for created_at), created_at, and updated_at. bridge_id and agent_session_id are never included — this verb does not expose routing/identity fields beyond what the pre-existing MCP surfaces have always shown.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Group by agent_id when presenting — a caller usually wants 'which claude_code sessions are up', not a flat list. Use session_label for the human-facing name and agent_instance_id when a reply or peer_send target is needed; the two are not interchangeable and a reply always needs the instance id. Do not infer liveness beyond 'this registry row currently exists' — a stale binding not yet swept still appears here.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Use agent_instance_id (never session_label) when addressing a specific instance via peer_send or similar routing. If the caller is looking for a role holder rather than an agent kind, this verb is the wrong tool — use peer_holds_role or the role-addressed send path instead; peer_list enumerates by agent_id/instance, not by role.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Read-only, unfiltered snapshot of the live peer registry on this solet. No identity resolution, no per-caller scoping, no write — the only failure mode is the messaging bridge itself being down.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: bridge.not_running: the agent messaging bridge is not active on this solet, so the registry could not be read at all. This is NOT an empty registry — no read happened, so an empty result would be misleading and is never returned for this reason.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: bridge.not_running: start the messaging interface (start_interface) and retry. There is no other error path for this verb — a successful call always returns a snapshot, even if that snapshot is empty (no peers currently registered).
